checkpoints.reason: The home hearth circulates, and the bridge met amber in an equal flame collision at G5. This is a consequential response and a natural first resolution.

continuations.intention: Close the remembered eastward edge at F5 as a deliberate boundary before the shared scar, then finish.

account.experience: I chose a direct flame bridge and then a small hearth beside home. Planning the four directed corners was the thoughtful part. The automatic outer forks also made circuits without my help, so merely getting a circuit feels too easy as a general objective.
account.noticedResponses: Amber sent flame back along the same row. At time 4 the equal fronts vanished into a shared scar at G5 just as my home loop closed.
account.narrativeOrConceptThatMattered: D5 began as a stone gate on the bridge and became the west-turning return of the home hearth. G5 changed from empty crossing to evidence of a failed meeting.
account.closure: The hearth project is resolved; the central bridge is a terminated encounter. I have no present desire to conquer the amber side.
account.renewedIntention: I do want one coda: use the remembered eastward passage at F5 to close the approach to G5, making the failed meeting an intentional boundary. Then leave this world.
account.repetition: The large automatic spread is already harder to inspect than the chosen four-place construction. I do not want to shepherd every branch.
account.wantAnother: Not another general expansion run right now.
account.actualContinuationReason: A single specific coda to give the central collision a chosen ending, rather than pursuing the invitation metric.

continuation.intention: Close the remembered eastward edge at F5 as a deliberate boundary before the shared scar, then finish.

report.experience: This AI protocol account had a short satisfying construction episode, followed by a chosen quiet ending. It is not evidence of human fun or human play duration.
chosenProjects: A flame bridge from the home shell through D5 toward the east
A clockwise four-place home hearth C4-D4-D5-C5
A remembered boundary at F5 after the central meeting failed
report.noticedResponses: The counterpart built its own circuit and sent flame west down the central row. Equal opposing flames made a shared G5 scar at time 4. At time 5 amber grew onto that scar and announced a Shell continuation west, while my remembered east edge at F5 was closed. I ended before seeing that announced action execute.
report.narrativeOrConceptThatMattered: D5 was first a stone bridge gate, then became the west-turning corner of my hearth. F5 was first the leading bridge path, then its remembered movement became the deliberate boundary beside the old contact. G5 retained both lineages in its history even after amber occupied it.
report.strongestEpisode: Closing the C4-D4-D5-C5 hearth at the same beat that the outward bridge met amber and stopped. The local creation succeeded while the outward invitation failed; that made a specific place worth leaving as it was.
report.thoughtful: I had to account for persistent friendly exits while arranging the ring; a right-turning seed alone would not overwrite the earlier eastward exits. Reusing the existing stone gate kept the ring connected to home.
report.routineOrWeak: The automatic initial forks produced several other circuits with no deliberate work, reducing the value of simply earning a living-circuit indicator. Branch growth rapidly produced a large board whose generic spread did not matter to my project. I felt no desire to manage all branches or alternate winning types until conquest.
report.unclear: I understood the exit rules better through the first few visible transitions. I did not evaluate long-run boundary stability or whether amber would eventually route around it.
report.closure: I finished at time 5 with the chosen home hearth alive, the approach to G5 closed, and the supplied eastern-reach invitation unmet. A terminated encounter was a valid ending for this project.
report.renewedIntention: After the first checkpoint I chose one specific coda, closing the remembered F5 east edge, and then carried out the planned finish. I have no further current project in this world.
report.repetition: No repeated wait or type-counter cycle was needed. I stopped before expansion and response management became the reason to continue.
report.wantAnother: Not another expansion run immediately. A scenario with a reason to shape one shared boundary or place could interest me more than broader reach.
report.actualContinuationReason: One voluntary coda gave the failed central meeting an intentional boundary. I did not continue for the initial metric, command allowance, or to tour features.
report.actualStopReason: The hearth and boundary were complete enough, and I preferred that quiet closure over inventing a conquest problem.
report.claimLimit: AI isolated public-interface play report; subjective language describes this protocol account, not measured human enjoyment.
